title: Thread death or reuse after an exception
context: When a task in a pool throws an exception, does the thread die or get reused?

source.title: JavaGuide (Snailclimb): Java concurrency questions (3 of 3)
source.note: Question and topic from this JavaGuide article. The answer is an original English write-up; see content/sources/javaguide/NOTICE.md.

answer: With `execute`, an uncaught exception ends the worker thread. The pool notices and starts a replacement, so the pool size stays the same, but the stack trace goes to the thread's uncaught handler. With `submit`, the exception is captured in the Future and rethrown by get(), so the worker survives. Either way, catch and log exceptions in the task yourself, and set an UncaughtExceptionHandler on the pool's ThreadFactory.

points.title: execute versus submit
points.why: execute loses the exception to the handler. submit hides it in the Future until get() is called.

points.title: Replacement thread
points.why: A dead worker is replaced, so the pool keeps its size.
